question: How does a faculty member mark daily attendance?
reference_answer: Faculty (also HOD or Institute Admin) go to Academic → Attendance Mark, pick the date, course and session (period), tick P for each present student or leave blank for absent, and click Save. Attendance can be edited until it is locked.

evidence.quote: Go to Academic → Attendance Mark . Pick the Date , the Course , and the Session (period 1, 2 …).

question: How do I freeze marks for a course, and what happens after freezing?
reference_answer: Only the COE freezes marks. First make sure every enrolled student has marks (check the Marks Coverage report), then on the Marks Entry page for the course and exam type click the orange Freeze button and confirm. After freezing, marks are read-only; changes need an Unfreeze by the COE.

evidence.quote: After freeze, marks become read-only. Edits need a special "Unfreeze" by the COE.

question: Why is the Freeze button greyed out?
reference_answer: Freeze stays disabled until every enrolled student has marks entered (marks with Present, or an Absent tick). The Marks Coverage report shows which students are still pending.

evidence.section: The Freeze button is greyed out. Why?
evidence.quote: Freeze needs every enrolled student to have marks (Present + marks OR Absent tick).

question: How does the COE generate marksheets for a semester?
reference_answer: The COE first makes sure all exam types for the semester are frozen, then goes to Post-Exam → Marksheet, picks the academic year, semester, program and branch, and clicks Generate (the system computes SGPA, CGPA and grades). Generate PDFs creates one printable marksheet per student and Print Bulk prints them all.

evidence.quote: Click Generate . The system computes SGPA, CGPA, grade for every student.

question: How is a revaluation request processed?
reference_answer: The COE or Exam Clerk opens Post-Exam → Revaluation, picks the request, checks that the revaluation fee is paid, and assigns a different valuer from the original. If the new marks are higher and change the pass result, the marks change and an amended marksheet is created; if they are the same or lower, the original marks stand (board policy varies). Resolve closes the request and notifies the student by SMS/email.

evidence.quote: Check the fee receipt — student must have paid the revaluation fee first.

question: How do I issue a Transfer Certificate to a student who is leaving?
reference_answer: An Institute Admin or Student Clerk opens Student → Student Master, finds the student, uses the More-actions (⋮) button, chooses Issue Transfer Certificate, enters a one-line reason and confirms. The system zips every uploaded document of the student into an archive and the student's status becomes TC_ISSUED.

evidence.quote: The student's status flips to TC_ISSUED .

question: How does the Student Clerk issue a bonafide certificate?
reference_answer: The Student Clerk goes to Student → Certificates, finds the request (or uses + Apply on behalf for in-person requests), picks the Bonafide type and adds the purpose, approves it and collects the fee at the Fees counter, then clicks Issue and Print. The certificate carries the Principal's signature image.

evidence.quote: Approve and collect the fee at the Fees counter. Come back, click Issue , then Print .

question: What types of late fine rules can be configured for fees?
reference_answer: An Institute Admin configures them under Fees → Late Fine Rules. Four types exist: FIXED (a flat amount), PER_DAY ((days late − grace days) × per-day amount, capped at MaxCap), PERCENTAGE (a percentage of the outstanding, capped at MaxCap) and SLAB (tiered amounts by day ranges). A nightly job (LateFineAccrualJob) writes accrued fines into the student's outstanding.

evidence.quote: a nightly Hangfire job ( LateFineAccrualJob ) walks every active structure and writes the fine into the student's outstanding.

question: How do I refund a single fee receipt?
reference_answer: A Fee Clerk or Institute Admin opens Fees → Fee Collection, opens the receipt, and clicks Refund (shown only for CLEARED receipts that are not cancelled or already refunded). The refund amount may be partial but cannot exceed the receipt total, the refund date cannot be earlier than the receipt date, and a reason is mandatory. Multi-receipt refunds use the consolidated Fee Refund form instead.

evidence.quote: Refund Amount — partial refunds allowed; cannot exceed the receipt total.

question: How do I turn on two-factor authentication?
reference_answer: Click your photo or name at the top right, choose Two-factor authentication, click Enable 2FA, scan the QR code with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or Authy), then type the current 6-digit code and click Verify & enable.

evidence.quote: Type the current code into the box and click Verify & enable .

question: How do I generate and export a report?
reference_answer: Click Reports in the left menu, pick a category (Student, Academic, Fees, Pre-Exam or Post-Exam) and the report, fill the filters (academic year, semester, program, branch, date range), click Preview, then Export as PDF, Excel (.xlsx) or Word (.docx).

evidence.quote: Click Preview to see the report on screen.

question: Where are library reports and what export formats do they support?
reference_answer: All library reports are under Library → Reports → <Category> (37 reports). Every report supports PDF, XLSX and DOCX export with an inline preview.

evidence.quote: All library reports live under Library → Reports → <Category> .

question: What does the Post-Exam module cover?
reference_answer: The Post-Exam module covers marks entry, moderation, marksheets, revaluation and photocopy requests.

evidence.quote: 9 Post-Exam POST_EXAM Marks entry, moderation, marksheet, revaluation, photocopy

question: Which module do I use to create the exam schedule, and who can do it?
reference_answer: Exam schedules are created in Pre-Exam → Exam Schedule by the COE, Exam Clerk or Institute Admin, adding one entry per exam with the academic year, semester, program, branch, course, exam type, date, start time, duration and maximum marks.

evidence.quote: Who can do this: COE, Exam Clerk, Institute Admin. Go to Pre-Exam → Exam Schedule .

question: Does Synchronik ERP support biometric attendance devices, and how do I connect one?
reference_answer: Yes. According to Synchronik's website, SackInfo integrates with attendance hardware including RFID, biometric devices, face-detection cameras and VTS. The help portal does not document the connection steps, so contact Synchronik support for setup.

evidence.section: Does the Synchronik ERP support biometric
evidence.quote: SackInfo integrates with attendance hardware including RFID, biometric devices, face-detection cameras and VTS

question: What does Synchronik do?
reference_answer: SyNchRoniK Inc. is an Indian company, established in Nagpur in 2001, that builds automation software only for educational institutions: campus ERP, library automation, OBE and payroll.

evidence.quote: It was established in Nagpur in 2001 to address the automation needs of educational institutions

question: What products does Synchronik offer?
reference_answer: SackInfo ERP (flagship campus management), Softlib (library automation), the OBE System, Payroll Software and Autonomous Modules.

evidence.quote: Softlib: library automation with RFID, OPAC, MARC cataloguing

question: How does the ERP keep each college's data separate?
reference_answer: The ERP is multi-tenant: every operational record carries an institute id and every query is scoped to the logged-in user's institute. Only the SuperAdmin role crosses tenants.

evidence.quote: Only the SuperAdmin role crosses tenants.
